item.title: Golden State wins first WNBA title in franchise history
item.description: The title was won in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history.

item.title: Inside the U.K. movement to pardon women executed for witchcraft centuries ago
item.description: In total, across England and Scotland, around 5,000 women convicted of witchcraft were executed, some by hanging and some by burning.

item.title: 2026 elections live updates: Trump supports Republicans with telerallies
item.description: The November 2026 midterm elections are just three days away. Candidates in key races — and President Trump — are making their closing arguments to voters.

item.title: Residents evacuated from Russia-occupied city back in Ukraine
item.description: The civilians traveled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus before returning to Ukraine, following a deal brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump.

item.title: Former nurse finds new calling caring for the dead
item.description: A former nurse who calls herself the "crazy cemetery lady" found a new calling: caring for the dead by restoring cemetery headstones, some of which are centuries old. Evyn Moon has the story.

item.title: French police clash with some protesters again as demonstrations continue
item.description: Police said about 70,000 people demonstrated in Paris alone. France's interior ministry said about 320,000 people rallied nationwide.

item.title: U.K. facing movement to clear convictions of women executed for witchcraft
item.description: There is a movement underway in the United Kingdom that is seeking official pardons for the thousands of women who were executed for witchcraft centuries ago. Holly Williams has the story.

item.title: Western U.S. contends with high tides, flooding
item.description: Record-breaking high tides are soaking portions of the West Coast, while storms caused heavy flooding that forced rescues in Arizona. Andrew Kozak has the forecast.

item.title: Residents evacuated from Ukrainian village under siege reunited with their families amid truce
item.description: Residents of a Russian-occupied village in southern Ukraine who have been living with limited food and electricity were evacuated and reunited with their families following a temporary ceasefire there negotiated by first lady Melania Trump. Those who chose to remain in Oleshky were given emergency supplies. Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Police clash with Paris protesters as demonstrations grip Europe
item.description: There was another wave of violence in Paris Saturday as anti-government protesters clashed with police. Demonstrations were also held across Europe.

item.title: El-Sayed asks fellow Democrat Stevens not to attend final campaign events
item.description: Stevens has demanded El-Sayed condemn an outside group's ad and apologize for comments he made about Israel. El-Sayed said Stevens is "intent on relitigating" their primary.

item.title: Video shows ICE agent pointing gun at bystander in Los Angeles
item.description: A new video shows an ICE agent pointing a gun at a bystander during an arrest operation in Los Angeles, sparking new outrage over the agency's tactics. Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: Travelers face sticker shock on airfare, gas prices as midterms approach
item.description: High airfares, driven by President Trump's Iran war, are causing some voters to suffer from sticker shock with midterms just days away. Akiko Fujita reports.

item.title: Trump rallies Republicans in Iowa and Kansas on last weekend before midterms
item.description: President Trump is holding previously canceled rallies in the key battlegrounds of Iowa and Kansas during the final weekend before the midterms. Olivia Rinaldi has the story.

item.title: Video shows immigration agents detaining man in North Hollywood
item.description: Los Angeles leaders are speaking out after video captured the moments when a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent pointed a gun at a bystander as a different man was detained in North Hollywood on Friday.

item.title: $6.3 billion Binance hack likely work of North Korea, experts say
item.description: A cyberattack on Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, was likely carried out by North Korea, according to a blockchain intelligence firm.

item.title: 10/31: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Trump rallies in Iowa, Kansas before midterms; Higher airfares, gas prices roil travelers.

item.title: Iran's supreme leader warns U.S., Israel against new attacks
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday no decision has yet been made on whether to renew hostilities with Iran.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Nov. 1, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include independent Sen. Bernie Sanders, Republican Rep. Mike Lawler and Democratic Gov. Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania.

item.title: DOJ calls Alaska Senate allegations "troubling," asks to segregate ballots
item.description: The top federal prosecutor in Alaska did not specify what crimes are being investigated by the Justice Department, saying he's "not making any assumptions on whether a crime has been committed or not."

item.title: Shootings kill 2 at Halloween Spirit stores in California, Michigan
item.description: Shootings on Friday night in California and Michigan at Halloween Spirit stores, a retailer selling costumes and decor, killed two people, authorities said.

item.title: Judge dismisses with prejudice Trump lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
item.description: In a 20-page ruling, U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the suit with prejudice, ruling that President Trump did not prove the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice.

item.title: Daylight saving time is almost over. Here's what to know.
item.description: Millions of Americans gain an hour of sleep this weekend when the time change commonly known as daylight savings ends for 2026, meaning clocks "fall back."

item.title: 17 theme park employees among 281 arrested in Florida sting, sheriff says
item.description: Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said 13 were Disney employees and four were Universal Studios employees among those arrested during a law enforcement sting.

item.title: Family of real estate CEO wounded in Toronto home invasion, officials say
item.description: A search is underway for three armed men who broke into a mansion in Toronto belonging to a real estate CEO in the early morning hours Thursday and attacked and injured the family inside, authorities said.

item.title: As Texas Dems predict a Hispanic wave, Hinojosa takes her pitch ringside
item.description: Days before Election Day, Texas Democratic gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa is stepping into the ring for a critical voting bloc in the Lone Star State: Hispanic men.

item.title: Pope meets Villanova and Notre Dame basketball teams at the Vatican
item.description: The teams are in Rome for the U.S. college basketball season opener — an event dubbed the Eternal City Tip-Off and created to honor the U.S.-born pope.

item.title: U.S. approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged his allies to speed up deliveries of the critical munition.

item.title: Meta settles social media addiction lawsuit, averting trial
item.description: Two plaintiffs alleged that Meta and Snap designed their social media platforms to foster addictive behavior.

item.title: High airfares are weighing on Thanksgiving travel plans this year
item.description: Average fares for the Thanksgiving holiday were up 31% in August from a year ago, according to aviation pricing data.
